Between a man and polytheism and unbelief stands the abandoning of prayer.
The five prayers, Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan expiate the sins between them, so long as major sins are avoided.
A sutra the height of a saddle's back suffices; the Prophet prayed facing a planted spear, staff or his camel, while people and animals passed beyond it.
Nearly of age, Ibn Abbas rode a donkey in front of the row as the Prophet led prayer at Mina, then joined it, and no one objected.
A worshipper must turn back, forcibly if needed, anyone passing before him; a passer knowing his burden would rather stand forty; the Prophet prayed near a wall or pillar.
Without a saddle-high sutra a passing woman, ass or black dog cuts the prayer; Aisha objected that the Prophet prayed at night while she lay between him and the qibla.
When supper is served as the prayer begins, eat first rather than hurry to pray; Aisha cited the Prophet: no prayer is right with food present or when nature calls.
Aisha had her copy of the Quran written 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer and the afternoon prayer', saying she heard it so from the Prophet.
The five daily prayers wipe away sins just as bathing five times a day in a river at one's door would leave no dirt.
For a man who kissed a woman a verse was revealed: pray, for good deeds remove misdeeds, for everyone; another seeking a prescribed punishment was pardoned for praying.
